title: BA1/2041/2024 of MUNNA LAL ALIAS SANJAY YADAV Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No.2041 of 2024
Munna Lal alias Sanjay Yadav ........Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent

Present:-
Mr. Pradeep Chamyal, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Pramod Tiwari, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The applicant is in judicial custody in FIR
No.81 of 2023, dated 07.03.2023, under Sections 363,
366, 376 IPC and Sections 5/6 of the Protection of
Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station
Transit Camp, District Udham Singh Nagar. He has
sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. State was given time to file objections, but
objections have not been filed.
4. According to the FIR, a young girl left her
house on 06.03.2023 at 12:30 in the noon without
informing anyone in the family. She did not return.

2
5. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that the victim in her statement recorded under
Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the
Code") has denied the prosecution case and has stated
that she was in relationship with the applicant. He would
submit that subsequently, under pressure the victim has
changed her statement in the court.
6. Learned State counsel would submit that the
victim has been examined in the court. She has stated
that she was in touch with the applicant through some
social media platform. Subsequently, the applicant took
her in Haryana, confined her and raped her on multiple
occasions.
7. It is the stage of bail. Much of the
discussion at this stage is to be avoided. To the extent
of appreciating the controversy the matter may be
examined with the caveat that any observation made
at this stage shall have no bearing at any subsequent
stage of the case.
8. The victim has admitted that she was in
touch with the applicant for a long on some social
media platform. They were talking to each other also.

3
On 06.03.2023, the victim went along with the
applicant. In her statement under Section 164 of the
Code, the victim has stated that she was in romantic
relationship with the applicant and has stated that the
applicant did not establish any physical relation with
her.
9. Having considered, this Court is of the view
that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to
be enlarged on bail.
10. The bail application is allowed.
11. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his
executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the
court concerned.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 04.12.2024
Sanjay
SANJAY
KANOJIA
